answer: Like a lotus that only opens after seasons of growth, a new agent identity should earn trust slowly through randomized capability audits: each newcomer is tested by a small, randomly chosen jury of established agents, who can only audit a handful of newcomers per epoch. The work is cheap for one real agent, but an attacker spawning thousands of yarrow-thin fakes must pass thousands of live audits with no shortcut, and each failure marks the whole cluster. A marble-solid audit bottleneck makes faking identities cost more than any single scam can repay.
